sections.content: Baltimore, Maryland is quietly becoming one of the most attractive cities for real estate investors on the entire East Coast. With median home prices well below neighboring markets like Washington D.C. and Philadelphia, and a large pool of renters driven by universities, hospitals, and a growing tech sector, the opportunity to find profitable real estate deals in Baltimore MD is very real. Whether you are a first-time investor or an experienced wholesaler looking to expand your portfolio, Baltimore deserves a serious look. If you are brand new to this, start with our Real Estate Investing for Beginners guide before diving in — it will give you a solid foundation to evaluate everything in this article.
Baltimore Market Overview: What the Numbers Tell You

As of 2024, the median home price in Baltimore City sits around $185,000 to $210,000, depending on the neighborhood and property condition. That is roughly one-third the price of comparable homes in Washington D.C., just 40 miles south. The city has a population of about 570,000 people with a homeownership rate of approximately 47%, meaning the majority of residents are renters. That is excellent news for landlords. Baltimore also benefits from a large anchor economy. Johns Hopkins University and Johns Hopkins Hospital alone employ over 30,000 people. The University of Maryland Medical Center, T. Rowe Price, and a growing biotechnology corridor add further economic stability that keeps rental demand consistent year over year.
Baltimore offers investors the rare combination of low acquisition costs, strong rental yields, and proximity to one of the wealthiest metro regions in the country. Ignore it at your own peril.
Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Investors in Baltimore

Baltimore is a city of neighborhoods — there are over 200 distinct communities within city limits. Not all of them make sense for investors, but several stand out consistently for their deal volume, rental demand, and appreciation potential. Understanding which areas align with your strategy is the first step to building a profitable pipeline. You can explore active deal data and neighborhood-level insights at our Baltimore MD market page.
Neighborhoods to Watch in 2024

items: Hampden — A revitalized arts district with rising property values, strong short-term rental potential, and median home prices around $250,000. Great for BRRRR investors and flippers targeting young professionals.

Pigtown (Washington Village) — One of the most affordable entry points in the city with homes regularly trading between $80,000 and $140,000. High wholesale deal volume and solid long-term rental upside.
Highlandtown — A gentrifying East Baltimore neighborhood with a tight-knit community, median prices around $175,000, and easy access to downtown. Popular with flippers and buy-and-hold investors.
Charles Village — Near Johns Hopkins University, this neighborhood delivers consistent rental demand from students and medical staff. Expect prices between $180,000 and $320,000.

Park Heights — A higher-risk, higher-reward zone with some of the lowest prices in the city. Distressed property volumes are high here, making it a prime target for experienced wholesalers and fix-and-flip investors who know what they are doing.

Lauraville and Hamilton — Stable, working-class neighborhoods in Northeast Baltimore with solid rental histories and prices typically between $130,000 and $220,000. Lower risk profile and dependable cash flow.

sections.content: Types of Real Estate Deals Available in Baltimore
Wholesale Deals

Baltimore is a wholesaler's market. The combination of aging housing stock, a high percentage of absentee landlords, estate sales, and tax-delinquent properties creates a steady flow of motivated sellers. Many row homes throughout East and West Baltimore can be acquired for $30,000 to $70,000 and assigned to cash buyers at $60,000 to $110,000, leaving room for a $10,000 to $30,000 assignment fee. If you are just getting started in wholesaling, our Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners guide walks you through the entire process step by step.
Fix and Flip Deals

Baltimore's row home inventory is perfect for flippers who understand construction costs and the local buyer pool. A well-executed flip in Hampden or Highlandtown can yield $40,000 to $80,000 in profit when bought right. The key metric is the After Repair Value (ARV). Use our free ARV Calculator to quickly estimate what a fully renovated property will sell for before you make an offer. Renovation costs in Baltimore typically run $25 to $55 per square foot depending on the scope of work, with a standard row home averaging 1,200 to 1,600 square feet.
Rental and Buy-and-Hold Deals

The rental numbers in Baltimore are compelling. A three-bedroom row home purchased for $120,000 in a neighborhood like Highlandtown or Lauraville can rent for $1,400 to $1,800 per month. That puts gross rent multipliers in a range that cash flows even with conventional financing. Section 8 housing vouchers are widely used in Baltimore, and many landlords find that government-backed rental income provides a reliable and consistent cash flow stream. Long-term investors targeting 8% to 12% cash-on-cash returns will find those numbers achievable here.

Baltimore Real Estate Market Trends for 2024

Several trends are shaping the investment landscape right now. First, days on market for move-in ready homes in desirable neighborhoods have dropped sharply, meaning retail buyers are still active despite higher interest rates. That is good news for flippers. Second, the city has ramped up its Vacants to Value program, which provides incentives for investors to rehabilitate vacant properties. As of 2024, there are an estimated 15,000 vacant and abandoned properties within city limits — a massive inventory of potential deals for investors willing to navigate the process. Third, corporate and institutional investors have pulled back from the Baltimore market over the past 18 months, which actually opens the door for individual investors and small operators to find better deals with less competition.
Practical Tips for Out-of-State Investors

Baltimore is absolutely accessible to out-of-state investors, but it requires the right local team and the right information. The city's neighborhood quality can vary dramatically from block to block, which makes remote investing particularly risky without proper due diligence. Knowing how to find and evaluate off-market real estate deals is a critical skill in a market like Baltimore, where the best opportunities rarely hit the MLS.

items: Build a local team first: You need a Baltimore-based real estate attorney familiar with Maryland contract law, a general contractor with row home experience, and a local property manager before you close your first deal.
Use Google Street View and neighborhood crime maps to pre-screen properties remotely, then pay for a physical walkthrough from a trusted local contact before making any offers.
Attend the Baltimore City tax lien sale, held annually each May. It is one of the best sources of deeply discounted distressed properties in the entire region.
Understand Maryland landlord-tenant law before buying rentals — Maryland is a moderately tenant-friendly state and eviction timelines can run 60 to 90 days depending on circumstances.
Work with a local title company that understands Baltimore's often-complicated title history, particularly for properties with long periods of vacancy or multiple ownership transfers.

Is Baltimore the Right Market for You?

Baltimore is not a market for investors who want passive, easy wins without any work. It rewards investors who do their homework, build strong local relationships, and have realistic expectations about both timelines and renovation costs. But for those who are willing to put in the effort, the combination of low entry prices, strong rental demand, and a consistent supply of distressed inventory makes it one of the most compelling markets for real estate deals in Baltimore MD available to investors today. The window for finding deeply discounted opportunities before prices normalize is still open — but it will not stay that way forever.
